players.product: NVLink copper cable cartridges, high-speed connectors and cable assemblies for NVL72 racks

quarterly_data.signal: Chairman and general manager Wang Laichun (2025 annual report briefing): memory supply constraints have slowed growth of mid/low-end and niche consumer-electronics products, though the company's broad business layout offset some of the pressure; because of memory supply it recently slowed its ODM phone business and shifted resources to AI PCs. He said on-device AI products are proliferating but none has yet reached volumes of ten million units.

Margins and costs (2025 annual report briefing): chairman Wang Laichun said Q1 2026 was affected by exchange rates and raw materials; board secretary Xiao Yunxi said the H1 2026 growth guidance below last year's pace reflects exchange rates, material price increases and many new-business introductions. On copper, Wang said cost increases on existing products are mostly absorbed by the company while new products pass them on to customers, alongside more futures-based material stocking; its connectors are customised, so there is no across-the-board price increase. Xiao said capital spending will not change significantly this year or next and capacity utilisation is fairly good.

Data center (2025 annual report briefing): chairman Wang Laichun said the data-center-related businesses are mostly at an early stage, with opportunities and challenges; its AI server business is relatively small and the focus is components. In copper (electrical) connection its technology and business perform well, though geopolitics adds commercial resistance; CPC has a chance to ramp next year, with progress as expected and test issues being resolved. In optical connection it is just starting: optical module revenue is very small relative to the market, its scale is small so supply is not a problem, and it will accelerate investment in step with business progress.

Acquisitions and automotive (2025 annual report briefing): chairman Wang Laichun said the Leoni integration is complete and very smooth, with business growth meeting and somewhat exceeding expectations; the acquisition from Wingtech is complete except for its India factory assets; the domestic plant acquired from Qorvo is integrating smoothly with business developing as expected; automotive electronics is growing as expected, the domestic market is highly competitive and the company is accelerating overseas expansion.

Footprint and regulation (2025 annual report briefing): chairman Wang Laichun said that apart from Southeast Asia the company is cautious about building new plants abroad, especially in Mexico where resources are unstable, and usually expands at existing sites to serve new customers and products; asked about the FCC withdrawing recognition of test labs in mainland China, he called it a sizable challenge shared by the industry chain that the company is still simulating, including possible alternatives and cost pass-through. Board secretary Xiao Yunxi said only some connectors and cables serve the commercial aerospace field for a North American customer, very small compared with consumer electronics.
